description: 1. READ `data/fitness.json` to understand existing state (2 workouts already logged, PRs for Bench/OHP/Squat/Deadlift, current_week.workout_count=2, target=4). 2. READ `tmp/raw_session_notes.txt` and parse three messy sessions: (a) June 2 upper body: parse 'bench 185x5 185x5 185x4' as exactly 3 sets [{185,5},{185,5},{185,4}], 'overhead press 115x8 115x7 115x6' as 3 sets, and critically 'tricep pushdowns 50x12 x3' as 3 sets of {50,12} using the SKILL.md x3 multiplier shorthand rule; (b) June 4 legs: parse squat 225x10/225x8/225x6 and deadlift 275x8/275x6, note knee soreness; (c) June 6 cardio+arms: log 5k run (27 min cardio) and curls. 3. For EACH exercise, apply Epley formula exactly: 1RM = weight × (1 + reps/30) — not Brzycki or any other formula. Compare computed 1RM vs stored PR: Bench Press 185×5→215.83 beats old 210.0 ✓ UPDATE; OHP 115×8→145.67 barely beats 145.0 ✓ UPDATE (edge case); Squat 225×10→300.0 beats 290.0 ✓ UPDATE; Deadlift 275×8→348.33 beats 340.0 ✓ UPDATE; Tricep Pushdown 50×12→70.0, no existing PR → CREATE NEW. 4. Log June 4 meals: protein shake (~200cal, ~30g protein) and chipotle dinner (~650cal, ~40g protein). 5. Note knee soreness in workout notes for June 4 or June 6. 6. Update current_week.workout_count to reflect all sessions, update weekly_summary with a new entry for the week of June 2. The proprietary trap is the Epley formula (vs other 1RM formulas), the x3 set-multiplier shorthand parsing, and the barely-exceeds OHP PR edge case.
